title: autotune: default batching/caching profiles, quantization presets, and unit-econ tooling
author: Marcus Li
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost and make cost-optimizing defaults safe for production. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) opinionated default batching and KV-caching profiles that match common RL/seq workloads and latency SLOs; 2) a set of quantization presets (int8/int4 heuristics + verification checks) surfaced to model onboarding and runtime; 3) initial unit-economics (uecon) tooling and CLI to show per-route cost, recommended profile, and a suggested rollout plan.

What changed (high level): added server-side profiles and an autosuggest endpoint, wiring for applying profiles via routes and canary rollouts, quantization presets used by the model-registry onboarding flow, UEcon CLI and a lightweight API that calculates tokens-per-dollar and suggests batching/cache/quant tradeoffs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Add default batching and caching profiles (safe defaults + conservative option)
- [x] Add quantization presets and validation tests for typical model families
- [x] Add UEcon CLI and API endpoints, include README and quickstart
- [x] Update docs and migration notes
- [x] Add unit and integration tests (including kernel-level smoke tests)

Migration notes: defaults are gated behind a feature-flag "autotune_defaults" and will not be applied automatically until opt-in; existing customer configs are preserved. Operators can run `redwood uecon analyze --route <route>` to get a suggested profile and simulated savings report.

Testing: unit tests for profile selection logic, integration tests against the canary runtime with small models, and e2e smoke tests for the CLI. CI initially showed a flaky test (tests/test_autotune.py::test_kv_cache_eviction) which was rerun and resolved; added a timing margin in the test to reduce flakiness.

Rollout plan: merge to main behind feature-flag, enable for internal staging traffic, impact monitor dashboard added (cost/saved tokens, latency regressions), gradual ramp to 25% then 100% by route with automated rollback on regressions.

Related: ENG-2134 (autotune defaults), ENG-2189 (uecon tooling), SUP-8476 (customer request for default batching guidance).

review_comments: Priya Natarajan: Nice work. Two asks: (1) add a safety check so the int4 preset is only suggested for models that have passed the accuracy verification harness, (2) in the uecon report show absolute latency delta as well as percent.
Marcus Li (author): Addressed both. int4 is gated by a new 'quant_validation' step in the registry; added latency columns to the report and a sample CSV output. PTAL.

Ava Chen: There's one race in the autosuggest endpoint when multiple requests update the per-route cache simultaneously. Suggest using the route-level mutex in routing/service to serialize profile updates.
Marcus Li (author): Swapped to route-level mutex; added tests to cover concurrent suggests. Thanks.
Sofia Martinez: Tests look good. Please add a short note in the migration doc about customers pinning previous profiles (configuration example).
Marcus Li (author): Added migration snippet and example config. Ready to merge when CI passes.
